investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-19T14:39–14:47Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that advertise it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes; if those nodes are cordoned, drained, or have the resource misconfigured, the effective schedulable pool is zero even if physical capacity exists.

Tertiary: A surge in concurrent remote-agent pod requests (from other workloads or a previous eval run that did not clean up) may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before this eval run started.

Lower confidence: A node-level configuration change (e.g., reduced kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity advertisement) could have shrunk the available resource pool without removing the nodes from the cluster.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval probe never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval probe called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and the pod remained unscheduled for 131–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never started, no agent was created, no runtime response was received, and all five required evidence fields were absent, causing the contract validation to fail completely.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe's agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message) and is consistent across all three sibling checks.

SECONDARY — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, even a partially-loaded cluster would appear at capacity.

TERTIARY — no preemption policy configured for eval probe pods: the scheduler reports 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', meaning lower-priority pods on the 2 eligible nodes cannot be evicted to make room. If eval pods had a preemption priority class, they could displace lower-priority workloads.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent demand: if other production or eval workloads are simultaneously consuming kata peer-pod VM slots, the 2-node pool may be structurally too small for the expected concurrency level.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and unallocated on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., a pod spec error or API-level failure) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state checks pass in a subsequent run while the cluster node count and kata VM allocation remain unchanged, the failure may have been transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent workloads) rather than a persistent capacity problem.

If the node affinity/selector rules on the pod spec are found to be incorrect and corrected, and the checks then pass without any change to kata VM capacity, the root cause would be the affinity misconfiguration rather than true resource exhaustion.
If a passing run produces all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) with no cluster changes, the failure was transient and not a structural capacity issue.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the failure would be localized to the runtime probe's specific pod configuration rather than a cluster-wide capacity problem.

Add a dedicated eval that verifies at least one remote-agent pod can be scheduled and reach Running state within a short timeout (e.g., 30s), separate from the full runtime response check, to isolate scheduling failures from runtime/API failures.

Add a node-affinity conformance eval that verifies the expected number of kata-capable nodes are present and correctly labeled in the cluster, catching cases where node pool changes silently reduce the schedulable node count.

Consider adding a preemption-policy eval or configuration check that verifies remote-agent eval pods have an appropriate PriorityClass assigned, ensuring they can preempt lower-priority workloads when VM slots are temporarily exhausted.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-19T14:39–14:47Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that advertise it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any new remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval probe never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval probe called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and the pod remained unscheduled for 131–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never started, no agent was created, no runtime response was received, and all five required evidence fields were absent, causing the contract validation to fail completely.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe's agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message) and is consistent across all three sibling checks.

SECONDARY — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, even a partially-loaded cluster would appear at capacity.

TERTIARY — no preemption policy configured for eval probe pods: the scheduler reports 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', meaning lower-priority pods on the 2 eligible nodes cannot be evicted to make room. If eval pods had a preemption priority class, they could displace lower-priority workloads.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent demand: if other production or eval workloads are simultaneously consuming kata peer-pod VM slots, the 2-node pool may be structurally too small for the expected concurrency level.
